# From hidden values to a reusable, certified probability law

Scientific continuation for Capital. 29 October 2026, Brisbane.

## Current result after the next construction and comparison

The strongest completed object is now an acquired candidate law together
with two measured quantities: a conditional mean residual R and a conditional
noise energy S. They support both direct reuse of the learned law and an
executable source correction at a stricter requested accuracy. Source values,
training, validation, preparation and correction are all charged. The current
result is conditional on a strictly contractive source and a useful constructed
candidate; it is not a general solution of dense native Gaussian-law sampling.

The first large validation below cost 1187841 values. Continuing past that
failure against the ordinary comparator produced two stronger constructions.
First, a 4096-query pilot acquired S<=.4796733159537619, replacing the
worst-case 54.21027964847543. A new U-statistic validation then certified
W2<=.4525404119140231 using 192513 complete original vector values. The old
worst-case bound on these same data gives .7407286944170575 and fails.

A simpler conventional paired-energy certificate is stronger on this fixture.
At a shared center take independent residuals D1,D2 and use

    Y+=(D1+D2)/sqrt(2),  Y-=(D1-D2)/sqrt(2),
    E||Y+||^2=2R^2+S,   E||Y-||^2=S.

One-sided Gaussian norm concentration bounds their population energy
difference. Its complete learned workflow costs 24577 original vectors
(8193 training plus 16384 fresh validation) and 2359392 scalar answers,
certifies per-output stationary W2<=.48980753486931167 with false-release
probability <=1/1024, and produces 8192 fresh candidate samples with no further
source values. The current ordinary global Gaussian-convolution sampler for
the same .5 target costs 393217 original vectors. The paired rule is adopted;
ordinary concentration and paired-moment identities are not novelty claims.

# Separate the learned dynamics from the noise control variate

29 October 2026, Brisbane. Ordinary proof and complete interface construction.
This nonlinear extension has not been executed in a new numerical fixture.
The affine specialization is the completed accuracy-interface experiment.

## 1. Representation change and target

The paired-energy certificate initially used an affine candidate because its
stationary law is an explicit Gaussian. The actual requirement is weaker:
an executable Lipschitz function of independent Gaussians, together with a
bound on its distance to a candidate stationary law. A finite contractive
nonlinear chain provides both. Also separate the candidate b, which models
the dynamics, from a matrix A, which controls native observation noise.

The target is the invariant law pi_g of

    K_g(x,.)=N(m_g(x),sigma^2 I),  m_g(x)=E g(x+G),

with G~N(0,I), sigma>0 and supplied global Lip(g)<=L<1. Only original
entire-vector values g(z) are available. After paid training, freeze an
evaluable b with a justified global Lip(b)<=beta<1 and an evaluable matrix A
with known ||A||<=a. Both may be learned from the same data. The candidate
kernel is directly K_b(x,.)=N(b(x),sigma^2 I), not a heat average of b.
This distinction eliminates a hidden candidate-mean oracle. Each kernel has
a unique invariant law in P2 by its strict contraction.

## 2. Actual finite candidate preparation

Execute Y_0=0, Y_(t+1)=b(Y_t)+sigma Z_(t+1) for exactly T steps. Let nu_T
be its law. As a map of the T independent Gaussian vectors, Y_T has global
Lipschitz constant sqrt(C_T), where

    C_T=sigma^2 sum_(j=0)^(T-1) beta^(2j).

Indeed, synchronous trajectories differ by at most
sigma sum_t beta^(T-t)||Z_t-Z'_t||; Cauchy--Schwarz gives the assertion.
This is an actual Gaussian preparation, not an inference of concentration
from an abstract Poincare constant.

Evaluate the known candidate at zero. Minkowski and stationarity give

    B_b=(||b(0)||+sigma sqrt(d))/(1-beta),
    [E_pi_b ||Y||^2]^1/2 <= B_b.

    W2(nu_T,pi_b)<=e_b=beta^T B_b.                 (1)

Every independent preparation pays T candidate steps and Td Gaussian
scalars. It uses no original source values, which does not make it free.

# Stricter stationary target: executed ordinary global-PW comparators

Both new comparators target per-output stationary W2 at most 0.1 for 8,192
outputs from the same fixed source (`d=96`, supplied `L=.5`, `sigma=1`,
source seed `2026102963`). They preserve all earlier code and receipts.

## Complete executed comparison

| Route | Values per output after preparation | Complete original vector queries | Complete scalar answers | Proved per-output W2 bound |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Standalone ordinary global PW, start at zero | 238 | 1,949,697 | 187,170,912 | 0.0998763231023892 |
| Same acquired candidate start, ordinary global PW | 191 | 1,589,249 | 152,567,904 | 0.09979577096414748 |
| Acquired integrated-noise control-variate correction | 52 | 450,561 | 43,253,856 | 0.09840593680410953 |

The second row is the stronger equally informed ordinary global-PW
comparison. It starts from exactly the acquired candidate law and initial
residual-radius certificate used by the corrected sampler. Its complete
count includes the same 24,577 acquisition queries, plus 1,564,672 newly
executed production queries. The acquired training anchor is included in
that acquisition; no duplicate anchor is needed.

The corrected route also pays 24,577 acquisition queries, followed by
425,984 correction queries. The equally informed global comparator uses
1,138,688 more native vector values, a factor 3.527267118103875 in complete
query cost. This is a comparison of explicit policies and their finite
schedule families, not a lower bound on other methods.
